title: The discovery of America
subject: histoire
description: On October 12, 1492, Christopher Columbus reached an island in the Bahamas that he believed to be Japan. A navigation error opens up globalization.

hero.hook: He was looking for Asia. It hit a continent that Europe had forgotten.

blocks.text: **October 12, 1492**, after more than two months in the Atlantic, a sailor from the Pinta shouts “Earth!” ". **Christopher Columbus**, Genoese in the service of Spain, lands on an island in the Bahamas which he names San Salvador. He believes he is reaching Asia.

This mistake will unite two hemispheres. Buoyed by the momentum of the [[The Spanish Reconquista (1492)]], the reconquest of Granada from the Muslims in the same year, the expedition marked, for Europe, the transition from the Middle Ages to the modern era.

sections.title: A road to the west, a big mistake

blocks.text: Columbus does not seek to prove that the Earth is round. [[Eratosthenes]], Greek scholar of the 3rd century BC. BC, had already calculated it. The real goal is economic: to reach spices and silk from the west, without going through the Ottomans who control the eastern routes.

blocks.caption: Christopher Columbus, Genoese navigator in the service of the Catholic Monarchs.

blocks.text: His mistake: underestimating the earth's circumference. It places Japan **4 500 km** from the Canaries, compared to almost **20,000** in reality. Portugal refuses. Isabella of Castile, Queen of Spain, accepts. Through the [[Santa Fe Surrenders]], a contract, Columbus becomes admiral, viceroy, and receives **10%** of the profits.
Columbus wrote of seeing mermaids in the Caribbean. They were manatees. He noted, disappointed, that they were much less beautiful than in the legends.

On **August 3, 1492**, three ships left Palos, Spain: the **Pinta**, the **Niña** and the **Santa María**. Thanks to the [[Pinzón]] family, rich local shipowners, the crew of **90 men** is experienced. The crossing lasts **70 days**. Columbus keeps two diaries: one real, the other falsified, to reassure his sailors.

blocks.caption: The Santa María, flagship of the 1492 expedition.

blocks.text: On **October 12**, he meets the [[Taínos]], indigenous inhabitants of the Greater Antilles. Convinced of being in India, he calls them “Indians”. He notes their gold and their apparent docility. The colonial gaze is already there.
La Niña was actually called *Santa Clara*. The Santa María was nicknamed *La Gallega*, because it was built in Galicia.

The arrival of Europeans triggered the **Columbian exchange**, a mass transfer of plants, animals and diseases between the two worlds. Towards Europe: potatoes, corn, tomatoes, cocoa, tobacco. Towards America: wheat, sugar, coffee, horses, cattle. The plates and landscapes on both sides change forever.

The price is terrible. Smallpox, measles, flu kill **50 to 90%** of indigenous populations in a century. Diplomatically, Spain and Portugal share the globe through the [[The Treaty of Tordesillas (1494)]], without consulting anyone.

events.title: Tordesillas
events.detail: Spain and Portugal share the world.

blocks.text: Columbus died in **1506** without admitting his discovery. It is [[Amerigo Vespucci]], a Florentine navigator, who understands that it is a “Mundus Novus”, a New World. In **1507**, the cartographer Waldseemüller named the continent **America**. The Florentine's first name enters the world map.

Brutal administrator in Hispaniola (present-day Haiti and Dominican Republic), Columbus even ended up sent back in chains. Beyond man, **1492** opens up globalization: American money flows in, the center of trade shifts from the Mediterranean to the Atlantic. Europe becomes the pivot of a system with four continents.
Columbus dies convinced that he has reached Asia. His error united two hemispheres and triggered an irreversible biological, economic and human upheaval.
